about: The prose rules scripts/prose.py applies, in ruletest.py's must_match / must_not_match shape (WD-7). Every regex or builtin rule carries at least one example it must fire on and one it must not; the helper checks both when it loads this file and refuses to run (exit 2) when any disagrees. A judgment rule has no pattern and is listed as not checked in every report. A rule's level per document type is strict (its severity applies), relaxed (reported as a candidate) or skip (not audited, and the report says so). Severity fail sets exit 1; candidate is listed and never changes the exit code. Nothing here edits a file.

levels.relaxed: reported as a candidate, whatever the rule's severity
levels.skip: not audited for this document type; listed under skipped, never counted as clean

doctypes.readme: a project's front page: current behaviour, first steps
doctypes.reference: reference pages, skill pages, API pages
doctypes.runbook: operational steps with expected results and recovery
doctypes.instructions: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and other instruction files
doctypes.as-built: a page that describes the system as built at one commit
doctypes.adr: decision records: history is the point
doctypes.changelog: changelogs: change narration is the point
doctypes.pr: a PR or issue body for a forge that shows single newlines as breaks
doctypes.reply: a review or chat reply posted to a forge or a chat thread
doctypes.ui: UI strings, one per line as key: text, or a flat JSON object

rules.why: a destination that shows single newlines as breaks turns a hard-wrapped paragraph into ragged lines; intentional breaks stay

must_not_match: publish.button: Publish
save.button: Save changes
rules.why: a button names the outcome it causes

must_not_match: publish.toast: Published
save.success: Changes saved
rules.why: a confirmation repeats the action's own name, so one action keeps one name through the flow

must_not_match: upload.error: The file is over 25 MB. Choose a smaller file.
save.error: Could not save: the server is offline. Try again in a minute.
rules.why: an error says what failed and one next step; an apology says neither
a universal (all, every, always, never) names the cases it covers or is narrowed; a pattern cannot tell a rule from an overclaim
a summary adds no claim, recommendation or caveat and settles no open question; preserve catches added numbers and names only
whether a documented flag or behaviour is merged and released needs the code and the release, not a pattern
a reply leads with the decision when the thread is visible and keeps every new measurement or its link
one action keeps one name from button to confirmation to error; the confirmation rule catches only the generic words
a first sentence that restates its heading adds nothing; which words count as a restatement is a judgment
a limit is stated once, as a scoped plain fact about what was not tested, never omitted and never wrapped in apology

reverted.false_positive: measured on westack's shipped pages during calibration: the bare form matched two present-state conditions and no narration, westack-build references/slices.md:53 (a test moved where the runner no longer collects it) and westack-debug references/flaky.md:3 (no longer timeout)
reverted.why: not adopted: diff-narration keeps 'no longer' only before a capability verb (supports, handles, accepts, returns, includes, requires), which matches neither page

gates_about: WD-9: a numeric prose gate (a rate per 1,000 words above which a rule fails) must be calibrated on the project's own existing docs. A gate names its rule, its threshold, a corpus manifest with that manifest's SHA-256, n (the number of corpus documents) and the registers they cover. The helper hashes the manifest and every file it lists before any run, and a mismatch stops the run (exit 2). It refuses a gate with n under 100 or a single register. No gate ships: every rule above is counted per occurrence, never as a rate.

selflint.about: WD-8: scripts/prose.py selflint ROOT lints westack's own Markdown. Each exclusion's hit count is reported beside the naive scan with no exclusions, so a dead exclusion shows zero. A fail rule at strict level counts against its ceiling (0 unless listed); a ceiling above 0 needs a log entry for every value it has held, and each entry may only lower it.

exclusions.not-shipped: files under an evals/ or tests/ folder: fixtures and answer keys hold bad text on purpose
exclusions.doctype-skip: a rule whose level is skip for the file's document type, such as change narration in a changelog
exclusions.code: a hit inside a code span or fenced block, for a rule that does not apply inside code (examples are quoted there)

ceiling_log.reason: first calibration: westack-verify references/claim.md:3 quotes a claim to be verified (this commit fixes the timezone bug); it is an example inside quotation marks, not narration
